title: Which Beatitude Defines You?
subtitle: Matthew 5. Which blessing names your season?
about: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus calls blessed the people the world usually overlooks: the poor in spirit, the grieving, the meek, the hungry for justice. Each beatitude names a real condition and attaches a real promise to it.

verses.text: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

questions.text: When you walk into church, what's underneath everything?

options.text: I have nothing to bring and I know it.
I'm carrying grief I haven't put down.
I'm hungry for something more.
I want to be clean. Really clean.

questions.text: What does kingdom-shaped strength look like to you?

options.text: Power held with a soft grip.
Bringing peace into rooms that don't want it.
Mercy when payback would be easier.
Standing for right even when it costs.

questions.text: Pick the prayer you've prayed most lately:

options.text: Comfort me. I can't pretend anymore.
Fill me. I'm so hungry.
Help me see You.
Make me a peacemaker, not a flame-thrower.

questions.text: How do you experience God's favor?

options.text: When I'm at the end of myself.
When I've been quietly hurt and stayed kind.
When I've taken hits for the right thing.
When my heart isn't divided.

questions.text: Which scene from the Sermon on the Mount lives in you?

options.text: Blessed are the poor in spirit.
Blessed are those who mourn.
Blessed are the merciful.
Blessed are the peacemakers.

questions.text: When you're wronged, your honest first instinct is...

options.text: Hold my fire and answer softly.
Forgive faster than I want to.
Pull out my journal and pray it through.
Sit in the silence until comfort comes.

questions.text: What blessing have you been quietly aching for?

options.text: The kingdom. I just need Him to be enough.
To inherit something only God could give.
To be filled and not run dry.
To finally see Him clearly.

questions.text: What would Jesus most likely say to your week?

options.text: Blessed are you who mourn, comfort is coming.
Blessed are you who make peace.
Blessed are you who hunger for right.
Blessed are you who've taken the hit.

poor-in-spirit.name: Poor in Spirit
poor-in-spirit.description: You know you don't have it all together, and that's exactly where the kingdom lives. The end of yourself is the place where Jesus turns out to be enough.

mourning.name: The One Who Mourns
mourning.description: You're carrying real grief, and you're not pretending it's fine. Jesus calls that blessed. Not because grief is good, but because comfort is coming and it has your name on it.

meek.name: The Meek
meek.description: You hold power with a soft grip. People mistake it for weakness, but it's real strength under control, and you'll inherit more than the loud ones ever will.

righteousness.name: Hungry for Righteousness
righteousness.description: You're starved for things to be made right, in you and in the world around you. That hunger isn't a flaw. It's the appetite God Himself is going to fill.

merciful.name: The Merciful
merciful.description: You give mercy faster than people expect. You've been forgiven much, so you forgive much, and the same mercy you've poured out is rolling right back to you.

pure-in-heart.name: Pure in Heart
pure-in-heart.description: You're learning to want one thing instead of ten. That undivided heart is going to see God in places other people miss Him entirely.

peacemakers.name: The Peacemaker
peacemakers.description: You walk into tense rooms and lower the temperature. You'll take the awkward seat in the middle if it means two people get reconciled, and that's exactly what gets you called a child of God.

persecuted.name: Persecuted for Right
persecuted.description: You've taken hits for doing the right thing. It's lonely and it hurts. But Jesus says heaven is on your side, and the reward is bigger than the cost.
